How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide for generating a **RESTful API request** in the **Cisco Nexus Dashboard** (v6.3.1) for the “get information of device connector versions” endpoint. --- ## 1️⃣ Where to find the API | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | Log into the Nexus Dashboard UI. | | 2 | From the left‑hand navigation pane, click **“Developer” → “API Explorer”**. | | 3 | In the **API Explorer** search bar, type **`device connector versions`** or the exact API name you mentioned. | | 4 | Click the matching result – you’ll see the full API definition (method, path, parameters, sample responses). | > **Tip:** If you’re not sure about the exact endpoint, you can also open the **“API Documentation”** tab (usually next to “API Explorer”) and browse the “Device Connector” section. --- ## 2️⃣ Generating the request Once you’ve opened the API definition: | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | Verify the **HTTP method** (GET, POST, etc.). For “get information of device connector versions”, it’s a **GET** request. | | 2 | Copy the **full URL** shown in the API definition. It will look something like:
`https://api.nexusdashboard.com/v1/device_connector_versions` | | 3 | If the API requires **query parameters** (e.g., `connector_id`, `status`, `page`, `size`), fill them in the parameter fields. | | 4 | Click the **“Generate Request”** button. The UI will automatically build a ready‑to‑send request. | | 5 | Review the generated request in the **Request Builder** panel. You’ll see:
• Method & URL
• Headers (including `Authorization: Bearer `)
• Query string (if any)
• Body (for POST/PUT; empty for GET) | | 6 | Click **“Send”** to execute the request. The response will appear in the **Response Viewer** panel. | --- ## 3️⃣ Authentication The Nexus Dashboard uses **OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens**. To obtain a token: ```bash curl -X POST \ https://api.nexusdashboard.com/oauth/token \ -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ -d "grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=&client_secret=" ``` Copy the returned `access_token` and paste it into the **“Authorization”** header field in the API Explorer (`Authorization: Bearer `). --- ## 4️⃣ Example cURL command If you prefer to run the request from the terminal, here’s a ready‑to‑copy example: ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://api.nexusdashboard.com/v1/device_connector_versions?connector_id=12345&page=1&size=50" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` Replace `` with the token you obtained earlier. --- ## 5️⃣ Using the `requests_get` function (Python) If you’d like to programmatically fetch the data using the tool you provided, just supply the URL (and optional params): ```python from functions import requests_get response = requests_get({ "url": "https://api.nexusdashboard.com/v1/device_connector_versions", "params": { "connector_id": "12345", "page": "1", "size": "50" } }) print(response) ``` > **Note:** The actual endpoint URL may differ slightly depending on your deployment. If you can share the exact URL or the API spec, I can tailor the code snippet more precisely. --- ### Quick Checklist - [ ] Logged into Nexus Dashboard v6.3.1 - [ ] Found the “device connector versions” API in API Explorer - [ ] Generated request with correct method, URL, headers, and params - [ ] Obtained OAuth bearer token - [ ] Executed request (via UI or cURL) - [ ] Reviewed response Let me know if you hit any snags or if you’d like a deeper dive into pagination, filtering, or error handling!
